title: Malacañang dares Alan Cayetano to donate P170,000 for national debt
summary: Malacañang on Tuesday challenged Senator Alan Peter Cayetano to donate P170,000 to help pay off the country's national debt, saying he could set an example for other Filipinos.

blocks.text: Malacañang on Tuesday challenged Senator Alan Peter Cayetano to donate P170,000 to help pay off the country's national debt, saying he could set an example for other Filipinos.
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said Cayetano's donation would encourage other Filipinos to voluntarily contribute to the government, on top of paying their taxes.
"Kung may mga mababait na puso at siya naman nagpasimula nito, mas maganda siguro makita mismo natin [kay Cayetano]," Castro said in a press briefing.
(If there are indeed kind-hearted people, and since he was the one who started this, perhaps it would be better for us to see him do it himself.)
Cayetano had floated the idea of Filipinos voluntarily contributing their P170,000 share of the country's P19.66-trillion national debt.
"We don't even have the mechanism for donating," Cayetano said. "What if we start the rich businessmen?"
However, the senator said the government must ensure that public funds and foreign loans are spent wisely to encourage Filipinos to contribute.

In a statement, Cayetano clarified that he was not proposing to impose an additional financial burden on the public but was exploring a voluntary mechanism for those willing and able to help reduce the national debt.

"There's no mechanism [for voluntary contributions] because no one thinks that anyone will donate because we think our government, not just this government, but government after government, it's just kung sino mas corrupt (who's more corrupt)," Cayetano said.

"The proposal to allow ourselves to pay part of our loan or get other people, one, is purely voluntary. Two, dapat gastusin nang tama ng gobyerno ang pera na nakokolekta. Three, i-monitor nang husto y’ung loans," he added.
(Second, the government should spend the money it collects properly. Third, loans should be closely monitored.)— MCG, GMA News
